title: Zeytinyagli Pirasa
subtitle: Turkish braised leeks in olive oil with rice
excerpt: Leeks braised slowly in olive oil with rice, carrot and a squeeze of lemon. Eaten at room temperature as a cold vegetable dish. One of Turkey's classic zeytinyagli, or olive oil dishes.
sourceNotes: Zeytinyagli means cooked in olive oil. This category of cold vegetable dishes is central to Turkish home cooking and meze tradition.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made several hours ahead. The dish needs time to cool fully and the flavours deepen as it rests.

content.text: This is a cold dish. The leeks braise gently in olive oil until very soft, then cool to room temperature before serving. Do not serve it hot; the texture and flavour are best at room temperature.

items.prepNote: white and pale green parts only, cut into 3cm rounds
peeled and cut into small dice

content.text: Warm 2 tablespoons of the olive oil in a large saucepan over a medium heat. Soften the onion and carrot for 6 minutes.
Add the leek rounds and stir gently to coat in the oil. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, lemon juice, sugar, salt and water. Stir once.
Pour in the remaining olive oil. Do not stir again. Place a circle of baking paper directly on the surface.
Cover with a lid and cook on the lowest heat for 35 minutes until the leeks are completely soft and the rice is cooked.
Remove from the heat. Leave to cool with the lid on for 30 minutes, then transfer to a serving dish.
Chill for at least 30 minutes more. Scatter over fresh dill just before serving.

items.symptom: The rice has turned to mush.
items.cause: Too much water or the heat was too high.
items.fix: Use the minimum amount of water next time. The dish should be moist but not soupy.

items.cause: They were stirred too much during cooking.
items.fix: Place the baking paper on top and resist stirring. The rounds should hold their shape if left undisturbed.

items.symptom: The dish tastes flat when cold.
items.cause: Cold food needs more seasoning than warm food.
items.fix: Add more lemon juice and salt just before serving. A drizzle of fresh olive oil over the top also helps.
